source: Built-in example; additive generalized DerSimonian–Laird random effects; normal confidence intervals.
plain: This analysis combined 8 independent contrasts to estimate 3 component effects. The model assumes that component effects add together on the supplied outcome scale. drug: evidence of a difference (the confidence interval excludes no effect). education: no clear evidence of a difference (the confidence interval includes no effect). exercise: evidence of a difference (the confidence interval excludes no effect). The direction and clinical importance depend on the outcome and scale supplied; this analysis does not establish causation.
methods: Independent contrast effects were fitted by inverse-variance weighted least squares under an additive component model. The design subtracts the components in intervention B from those in intervention A; control denotes the empty component set. Component labels are case-insensitive. Effects and SEs are used on the supplied scale without transformation or back-transformation. The generalized DerSimonian–Laird moment estimator uses the common-effect residual Q and residual degrees of freedom, with denominator equal to the sum of weights minus the trace of the common-effect covariance times the design cross-product weighted by squared inverse sampling variances. The between-contrast variance is truncated at zero; a numerically nonpositive denominator also gives zero. Random-effects weights are the inverse of sampling variance plus between-contrast variance. With zero residual degrees of freedom, heterogeneity is not estimable and sampling variances alone are used. Normal Wald 95% confidence intervals use the estimate plus or minus the standard normal critical value times its SE. Combination effects sum the component estimates, and their variances include all component covariances. No hypothesis tests, prediction intervals, automatic interactions or multi-arm covariance correction are computed. Only independent two-arm contrasts are supported. Analyses were run in allmeta component-nma <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: The additive model included 8 contrasts and 3 components. Component effects: drug = −0.289 (SE 0.058; 95% CI −0.402 to −0.175). education = −0.108 (SE 0.097; 95% CI −0.298 to 0.082). exercise = −0.177 (SE 0.053; 95% CI −0.280 to −0.074). Implied intervention effects versus control: drug = −0.289 (95% CI −0.402 to −0.175). drug+education = −0.397 (95% CI −0.572 to −0.222). drug+education+exercise = −0.574 (95% CI −0.742 to −0.405). drug+exercise = −0.466 (95% CI −0.630 to −0.302). education+exercise = −0.285 (95% CI −0.459 to −0.111). exercise = −0.177 (95% CI −0.280 to −0.074). Common-effect residual Q = 0.120 (df = 5). Between-contrast variance τ² = 0.000.
